accepted.s: Which one of the following policies specified a target of raising Gross Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD) to 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Five Year Plan?
accepted.x: The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 targeted an increase in GERD to 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Plan. The 1958 and 1983 policies did not state a numerical GERD target.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy linked to the specific numerical target.
accepted.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

accepted.s:
With reference to the GERD targets in India’s science and technology policies, consider the following statements:
1. The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 stated no numerical GERD target.
2. The Technology Policy Statement, 1983 stated no numerical GERD target.
3. The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 targeted GERD of 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Plan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 1958 and 1983 policies had no numerical GERD target, while the 2003 policy set a 2% of GDP target by the end of the Tenth Plan.
accepted.tq: Check each policy separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

accepted.s: The Science, Technology and Innovation Policy, 2013 envisaged GERD at 2% of GDP with which of the following additional features?
o: Private-sector spending being limited to one-fourth of public spending
GERD being financed exclusively by the Union Government
Abolition of public expenditure on research
accepted.x: The 2013 policy envisaged GERD at 2% of GDP, with private-sector spending matching public spending.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the matching private-sector contribution from exclusive public financing.
accepted.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal GERD-related target associated with the draft Science, Technology and Innovation Policy, 2020?
o: To raise GERD to 2% of GDP only once by the end of the Tenth Plan
To double the number of FTE researchers, GERD and the private share of GERD every five years
To maintain the existing level of GERD for five years
To eliminate private-sector participation in research funding
accepted.x: The draft STIP 2020 proposed doubling full-time-equivalent researchers, GERD and the private share of GERD every five years.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive repeated-doubling target to identify the policy.
accepted.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

accepted.s: India’s GERD reached approximately what share of GDP in FY 2023–24, described as a 15-year high?
accepted.x: GERD reached about 0.84% of GDP in FY 2023–24, a 15-year high. The national aim nevertheless remains 2% of GDP.
accepted.tq: Separate the latest achieved value from the long-term national target.
accepted.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the 2026 recommendations concerning research and innovation funding?
o: GERD should reach 2% of GDP within four to five years through greater private-sector participation, along with creation of NISPG and Vigyan Nidhi
A National Institute for Science Policy and Governance should be abolished and fellowships decentralised
GERD should remain below 1% of GDP and public funding should replace private funding
The target is to double GERD within one year through the existing fellowship system only
accepted.x: The recommendations called for GERD to reach 2% of GDP within four to five years through the private sector, proposed NISPG, and suggested a unified fellowship called Vigyan Nidhi.
accepted.tq: Match the recommendation package rather than isolating one proposal.
accepted.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Research, Development and Innovation Fund:
1. It has an approved size of ₹1 lakh crore.
2. ₹20,000 crore was provided for FY 2025–26.
3. It is intended to boost private research and development.
4. It is operated through a Special Purpose Fund in the ANRF.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The RDI Fund has a ₹1 lakh crore size, includes ₹20,000 crore for FY 2025–26, promotes private R&D and operates through a Special Purpose Fund in ANRF.
accepted.tq: Test the fund’s size, annual allocation, purpose and institutional channel together.
accepted.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

accepted.s: The Research, Development and Innovation Fund is intended to be implemented over which period according to the stated estimates?
o: Six years, with another estimate referring to seven years
accepted.x: One estimate describes implementation over six years, while another source refers to seven years. The stated material therefore records both estimates.
accepted.tq: Watch for closely related duration figures rather than assuming a single period.
accepted.sec: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

accepted.s: The Prime Minister’s Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council (PM-STIAC) was set up in:
accepted.x: PM-STIAC was set up in 2018.
accepted.tq: Directly associate the advisory council with its establishment year.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s: Who chairs the Prime Minister’s Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council?
accepted.x: PM-STIAC is chaired by the Principal Scientific Adviser.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who chairs this body?’ institutional-role test.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser:
1. It was created in 1999.
2. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the first Principal Scientific Adviser.
3. The Principal Scientific Adviser is the chief science and technology adviser to the Prime Minister and the Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The office was created in 1999, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was its first holder, and the PSA advises the Prime Minister and Cabinet on science and technology.
accepted.tq: Combine establishment, first office-holder and functional role in one institutional question.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a statutory body established under the ANRF Act, 2023?
accepted.x: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) is a statutory body established under the ANRF Act, 2023.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a statutory body created by legislation from advisory offices and missions.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the leadership structure of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation?
o: The Minister of Finance is its President and the Minister of Education is its sole Vice-President
The Prime Minister is its President and the Ministers of Science and Technology and Education are Vice-Presidents
The Principal Scientific Adviser is its President and the Cabinet Secretary is its Vice-President
The President of India is its President and the Prime Minister is its Vice-President
accepted.x: The Prime Minister is the President of ANRF, while the Ministers of Science and Technology and Education are its Vice-Presidents.
accepted.tq: Use the constitutional-style office hierarchy to discriminate between authorities.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about ANRF is NOT correct?
o: It provides strategic direction for research and innovation.
It pools public and private research and development resources.
Its entire proposed ₹50,000 crore funding for 2023–28 is to come from non-government sources.
It subsumed the Science and Engineering Research Board.
accepted.x: The proposed funding is ₹50,000 crore for 2023–28, of which about ₹36,000 crore is expected from non-government sources; therefore, the entire amount is not expected from non-government sources.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect funding-composition statement rather than the incorrect institutional function.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s: The ANRF is associated with which of the following financial and institutional roles?
o: Replacement for the Department of Biotechnology
Custodian of the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund
Authority for fixing the national GERD percentage by constitutional amendment
Exclusive custodian of the Atal Innovation Mission budget
accepted.x: ANRF is the custodian of the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund. It is not a replacement for DST or DBT and does not fix GERD through constitutional amendment.
accepted.tq: Link the fund with its designated institutional custodian.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the institution with its role or establishment detail?
o: DST — established in 1986 as the parent department of CSIR
DBT — established in 1971 as the nodal department for science policy
DSIR — established in 1985 and functioning as the parent department of CSIR
CSIR — established in 1971 as the Department of Biotechnology
accepted.x: The Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) was established in 1985 and is the parent department of CSIR. DST was established in 1971, DBT in 1986 and CSIR in 1942.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure institutional-year pair and reject swapped departments.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Department of Science and Technology was established in 1971.
2. The Department of Biotechnology was established in 1986.
3. CSIR was established in 1942.
4. The Secretary of DSIR is the Director-General of CSIR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. DST dates from 1971, DBT from 1986, CSIR from 1942, and the Secretary of DSIR serves as the Director-General of CSIR.
accepted.tq: Verify dates and the parent-department relationship independently.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s: PM-STIAC framed nine technology missions during which period?
accepted.x: PM-STIAC framed nine technology missions between October 2018 and January 2019.
accepted.tq: Use the narrow date range to distinguish the council’s mission-framing phase.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s: During India’s chairship of BRICS science and technology cooperation, which two organisations act as India’s lead agencies?
accepted.x: CSIR and the Department of Biotechnology act as India’s lead agencies for BRICS science and technology cooperation during India’s chairship.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct pair of lead agencies rather than a general policy body.
accepted.sec: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

accepted.s: The National Innovation Council, established in 2010, was associated with which of the following?
o: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and the management of defence production
Sam Pitroda and the promotion of inclusive innovation
The Principal Scientific Adviser and the regulation of higher education
NITI Aayog and the preparation of the Five Year Plans
accepted.x: The National Innovation Council was established in 2010 under Sam Pitroda, with inclusive innovation as its goal.
accepted.tq: Pair the body with its chairperson and distinctive objective.
accepted.sec: Decade of Innovation (2010-2020)

accepted.s: Which of the following was a feature of the National Innovation Council’s approach?
o: Replacement of all state science councils by one central council
Withdrawal of innovation initiatives from the private sector
Restriction of innovation activities to defence laboratories
Creation of state and sectoral innovation councils
accepted.x: The National Innovation Council promoted inclusive innovation through state and sectoral innovation councils.
accepted.tq: Select the institutional mechanism that follows the stated inclusive-innovation objective.
accepted.sec: Decade of Innovation (2010-2020)

accepted.s: The Decade of Innovation led into which major policy, in which innovation was made central?
accepted.x: The Decade of Innovation led into the Science, Technology and Innovation Policy, 2013, which placed innovation at the centre of policy.
accepted.tq: Follow the policy sequence from the innovation decade to the later policy.
accepted.sec: Decade of Innovation (2010-2020)

accepted.s: The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 was introduced during which Five Year Plan?
accepted.x: The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 came during the Second Five Year Plan, which covered 1956–61.
accepted.tq: Place the policy within the correct Five Year Plan period.
accepted.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

accepted.s: The Defence Research and Development Organisation was formed by merging which of the following?
o: TDE, DTDP and the Defence Science Organisation
accepted.x: DRDO was formed by merging the Technical Development Establishment, the Directorate of Technical Development and Production, and the Defence Science Organisation.
accepted.tq: Test the formation history through the exact component organisations.
accepted.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

accepted.s: Which organisation is the nodal agency for improving India’s Global Innovation Index rank and also publishes the India Innovation Index?
accepted.x: NITI Aayog is the nodal agency for improving India’s GII rank and publishes the India Innovation Index.
accepted.tq: Identify the agency from its paired ranking and index functions.
accepted.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

accepted.s: The third edition of the India Innovation Index, published by NITI Aayog, was released on:
accepted.x: The third edition of the India Innovation Index, dated 2021, was released on 21 July 2022.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the edition year from the actual release date.
accepted.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

accepted.s: Which of the following is hosted by NITI Aayog?
accepted.x: NITI Aayog hosts the Atal Innovation Mission.
accepted.tq: Match the mission with its host institution.
accepted.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

accepted.s: According to the Ease of Doing R&D in India report, approximately what share of ANRF funds goes to IITs?
accepted.x: The report states that approximately 80% of ANRF funds go to IITs and also points to slow approvals.
accepted.tq: Identify the magnitude of the institutional funding concentration.
accepted.sec: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

accepted.s: Which of the following is a role of State Councils of Science and Technology such as APCOST?
o: Issuing national patents and regulating all Union laboratories
Framing state science and technology policy, providing research grants and popularising science
Serving as the statutory governing council of ANRF
Determining India’s Global Innovation Index methodology
accepted.x: State S&T councils frame state S&T policy, provide research grants and popularise science. They do not perform the national statutory functions of ANRF or NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Apply the state-level institutional role to the functions listed.
accepted.sec: AP State Council of Science and Technology (APCOST) - state-level role

accepted.s: APCOST functions under which department of the Government of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Industries, Commerce and Information Technology Department
Higher Education and Skill Development Department
Environment, Forests, Science and Technology Department
accepted.x: APCOST works under the Andhra Pradesh Environment, Forests, Science and Technology Department.
accepted.tq: Use the department-name distinction to avoid a neighbouring-department trap.
accepted.sec: AP State Council of Science and Technology (APCOST) - state-level role

accepted.s: State science and technology councils such as APCOST receive support under which programme of the Department of Science and Technology?
accepted.x: APCOST and similar state councils receive support under the Department of Science and Technology’s State S&T Programme.
accepted.tq: Match the state institution with the correct DST support programme.
accepted.sec: AP State Council of Science and Technology (APCOST) - state-level role

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding state science and technology councils:
1. They can provide research grants.
2. They can popularise science.
3. The Tamil Nadu State Council for Science and Technology works on translating academic research into use.
4. APCOST’s founding year and current programmes are specified as established features of its institutional role.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The stated institutional information does not specify APCOST’s founding year or current programmes, so statement 4 is not correct.
accepted.tq: Separate stated functions from details that are not established by the institutional description.
accepted.sec: AP State Council of Science and Technology (APCOST) - state-level role
